aiSymmetry: NPC attempts pass the same stages minus the gate (device check, block, throw); a refused NPC device has attempted nothing — witnesses (#272) read only what the throw stage produced, in both directions
cancelLaw: the cancel input at the prompt equals NO, whole and silent (no item, no turn, no deed, no record); a cancel before the prompt is ordinary menu behaviour; no input of any class means anything at the gate but the answer visibly given

integrityProperty.statement: no input path — misclick, buffered input, menu shortcut, remapped control — may produce a stage-5 throw at a prompt-class target without a recorded YES at the gate
integrityProperty.status: a data-integrity property, stated as a test (STAGING step 4): a scripted input sweep over prompt-class targets must yield zero ungated throws
integrityProperty.violationClass: the system's central integrity defect, not a balance issue

noBuffering: inputs queued before the prompt appears cannot answer it — the gate reads a fresh input made while it stands; the confirming press is consumed by the prompt and cannot leak into the throw stage as a second command
note: This spec is why #269's addendum claim ('there is no accidental-theft state anywhere in the system') is a fact rather than a slogan: the prompt is a gate the throw is built behind, not a warning attached to it.
pipeline: 1. Targeting — the throw input names a field target (#10 ring / #165 bag-command grammar; legality read at command time)
2. Device check — item record read (snag class, reader presence); refusal classes evaluated here (#351) — a refusal ends the input, spoken and unconsumed
3. The block — an ordinary item at an owned target stops at #268's owned-block, refused before any roll and before any prompt
4. The conscience gate — a snag-class item at a prompt-class target raises #347/#349's prompt; the throw does not exist until this stage completes with YES
5. The throw — #268's math runs; #269/#348 write what happened
